reading: The input is the left half of an outline shape. Mirror it across the right edge of its box to close the outline, then output only the interior of the closed outline, filled with the shape colour (the outline itself is erased).

slots.half: the single fg object (left half of an outline)
slots.axis: vertical line just right of the object's bounding box (no shared column)
slots.fill: cells strictly inside the mirrored closed outline, row by row
slots.rest: outline and everything else cleared to background

why: on every pair the output's fg cells are exactly the interior of the outline formed by the input half plus its reflection across the box's right edge

reading: A straight arm of 2s is attached to a single 5. The arm is rotated 90 degrees clockwise about the 5 (drawn as 2s), and the cells of the old arm become 3.

slots.arm: the run of 2s adjacent to the pivot
slots.new arm: same length, rotated 90 degrees clockwise around the pivot, colour 2

why: on every pair the arm direction left->up, right->down, up->right, down->left (clockwise), same length, old arm cells become 3

reading: Each square outline of 5 has its hollow interior filled with a colour set by the interior size: 1x1 -> 6, 2x2 -> 7, 3x3 -> 8.

slots.region: interior (enclosed background) of each 5 outline object

why: every enclosed interior is filled, colour depends only on its size; outlines and outside unchanged

reading: A 1xN row with a central 2 becomes an NxN grid: the 2 draws a V of two diagonals down to the side borders, and inside/under its left arm parallel down-right diagonals of 1 are drawn every 4 columns (lines with col-row congruent to centre mod 4), never overwriting 2s.

slots.size: output is N x N where N is the input width
slots.V: 2 at (r, c0-r) and (r, c0+r) for r = 0..c0, c0 = centre column
slots.lines: colour 1 on cells with (col-row) = c0 - 4k, k >= 1, from the left arm downward-right to the border

why: on every pair the 2s form the V from the apex and the 1s are exactly the down-right diagonals spaced 4 apart starting below the left arm

reading: Every row or column that is entirely 0 is painted with 2; all other cells stay.

new_rows.name: empty_line
new_rows.datalog:
nz_row(Y) :- px(Y, X, C), C > 0.
nz_col(X) :- px(Y, X, C), C > 0.
empty_line(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !nz_row(Y).
empty_line(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !nz_col(X).

why: the cells of all-0 rows and columns become 2 and nothing else changes

reading: The 3x3 input is tiled into a 9x9 grid: block (i,j) is a copy of the input where input cell (i,j) has the most common colour, else empty.
why: blocks holding a copy are exactly the positions of the input's most frequent colour
invariants: the unit is the whole input

reading: The grid is split into vertical panels by all-background columns; each panel has one pattern colour. In each panel the background cells take the pattern colour of the next panel to the right (the last panel takes the first panel's colour); separator columns stay.

slots.panels: column stripes separated by full background-colour columns
slots.subject: background cells inside each panel
slots.colour: the fg colour of the next panel, cyclically (last -> first)

why: on both pairs panel k's background becomes panel k+1's colour (wrapping), pattern cells and separator columns unchanged

reading: Each hollow square points toward a bar of 1s on the border in line with it; the square is repeated end to end (period = its size) from itself to that border, the last copy cut at the border, and the 1-bars are erased.

slots.direction: toward the border where a 1-bar lies on the same rows/columns as the square
slots.copies: translate by the square's size repeatedly until the grid edge, cropping the last

why: each square's copies tile contiguously along its row or column band from the square to every border carrying an aligned 1-bar

reading: Some rectangles have a thin one-cell-wide tail; each such rectangle slides in the tail's direction by the tail's length and the tail disappears. Rectangles partly hidden under others are restored as full rectangles; the moved shape is drawn on top.

slots.subject: each rectangle with a protruding thin line
slots.others: tail-less rectangles stay, completed to full rectangles where occluded

why: on every pair each tailed rectangle's new position equals old position shifted by tail length toward the tail, keeping its shape

reading: Tile the input 3x3, then for every coloured cell paint the background of its whole row 1 and put 3 at its up-left and down-right diagonal neighbours (if inside the grid).

slots.row: every background cell in a row containing a coloured cell becomes 1
slots.diagonals: cells at (r-1,c-1) and (r+1,c+1) of each coloured cell become 3, clipped at the grid edge

why: on every pair the output equals the 3x3 tiling plus 1-rows through the coloured cells and 3s on their up-left/down-right diagonals
